summary: Adversarial test of multi-tenant org isolation (iter393). The core DB proxy works: cross-tenant GET/PUT/DELETE by id returns 404 and the record survives on members, events, tasks, invoices, hr payslips, social-work cases, expenses, donations, bookings and locations. organization_id in a body, query or $set is stripped. A new org starts empty with only its own campus. Suspend blocks login and revokes live tokens, reactivate restores access, delete needs suspend plus the slug, and export/import gives a separate org with a fresh id. Registry routes return 403 for org admins. The super-admin picker token gets 403 on data routes, and entering a new org replaces the old one. Hostname-gated login works. 58:12 Global regression is green and public pages work. The UI flows work: picker, banner, Organisations page with counts and Open/Export/Suspend, create via UI, suspend, delete-with-slug. However I found 4 CRITICAL/HIGH holes that break tenant isolation outside the proxy: (1) any org admin can create or promote a super_admin and take over every tenant; (2) /api/auth/google accepts unsigned JWTs, which is a full account takeover; (3) entire routers have no auth, so they run in the default org for everyone; (4) WebSocket presence, broadcasts and chat delivery cross tenants. The same-email-in-two-orgs login is also broken on the shared host. 37/41 pytest passed (all 10 iter392 tests included).

critical.issue: An ordinary org admin (admin@lubwamas.org) can create a user with role 'super_admin', or promote an existing user to it, and gets 200. That account can log in, list /api/organizations (200), enter 58:12 Global, export it, suspend it or delete it. This defeats all isolation. Reproduced live and cleaned up.

emergentintegrations.llm.google_auth does not exist, so the ImportError fallback base64-decodes the JWT payload WITHOUT verifying the signature. A forged token {email:'admin@5812uganda.org'} returned a valid admin session (/auth/me and /members both 200). Unknown emails create a pending Guest user in whatever org is pinned, and ?org=<slug> picks the tenant. Reproduced; the forged user was deleted.

Code review, not executed (destructive). These routes have no auth. POST /api/seed?org=<slug>, or a call on a tenant's hostname, inserts admin@5812global.org / Admin@1234 with role admin into that tenant if it is missing, plus demo members, locations and notifications with fixed ids. That is anonymous takeover of any new tenant (Lubwamas qualifies).

These routes never call get_current_user, so the middleware pins the DEFAULT org for everyone. Anonymous GET /api/calling/extensions and /calling/contacts return 58:12 staff names, emails, roles and forward_to phone numbers. A Lubwamas user using calling or conferences reads and writes 58:12 Global data. /presence/online-users also pops in-memory presence entries for users outside the pinned org, wiping other tenants' presence.

ConnectionManager is process-global. online_users, user_online/user_offline and presence_update are broadcast to every tenant: a Lubwamas socket received the 58:12 admin's id, and the reverse. access.py ws_manager.broadcast sends guest-visit notifications (guest name, location) to all tenants. Chat conversation participants are not checked against the org: Lubwamas admin created a conversation with the 58:12 admin's id and the message was pushed live to that admin's socket. The WS also has no token auth, so anyone can connect as any user_id (pre-existing).

The identity lookup uses raw_db.users.find_one, i.e. the FIRST match across tenants. With the same email in two orgs and different passwords, only one person can ever sign in on the preview host; the other gets 401. Reproduced: DupA 200, DupB 401. After an export→import, the copied users (same email and hash) always land in whichever org Mongo returns first. Fix: find all matching identities, verify the password against each, and require org choice or hostname if several match.

minor.issue: Returns 200 (PUT returns null) for another tenant's location id. Nothing is modified (proxy-scoped), but it should be 404.

Copies is_default from the source org. Importing a 58:12 Global export would create a second is_default org, and the middleware fallback would pick one arbitrarily. Uploaded files on disk are not part of the export.

active_organization_id persists on the user record and logout does not clear it. requires_org_selection is only returned the first time; later logins drop straight into the last org, with no picker. The super admin's active org is also shared across all of their browsers and sessions.
Pre-auth and scoped to the host-resolved org. On the preview host, non-default tenants cannot use PIN login and silently get no reset email. The reset email is hardcoded with '58:12 Global' branding.

Falls through to the raw collection for bulk_write, find_one_and_replace, find_raw_batches and aggregate_raw_batches, and watch/estimated_document_count are listed as passthrough. None are used today, but each one would be an unscoped hole. aggregate() only scopes the base collection: $lookup, $unionWith, $graphLookup and $facet sub-pipelines into other collections are unscoped (used in calling.py's users $lookup). A list-style (pipeline) update with upsert is not stamped.

ui_bugs.issue: /organizations has no client-side role guard. An org admin can open it, sees the Import and New organisation buttons, and the sidebar highlights 'Organisations'. The backend correctly returns 403 ('Super admin only' toast).

issues: Page container has no horizontal padding: the title and cards sit flush against the sidebar edge, and the Import / New organisation buttons touch the right viewport edge. Other pages use roughly 20px padding.
The campus dropdown under the active-org banner renders empty, with no campus name, for the super admin in both orgs.

action_items: CRITICAL: Block assigning role super_admin (and any role above the caller's own) in admin user create/update, member→user conversion, invites and bulk import. Only an existing super_admin may grant it. Audit existing users for role=super_admin.

CRITICAL: /api/auth/google must verify the Google ID token signature (google-auth id_token.verify_oauth2_token with the client id) and remove the unsigned base64 fallback. Apply the org gate (_resolve_login_org and the suspended check) there too.
CRITICAL: Remove the /api/seed* routes or protect them with require_super_admin. They must never run under an arbitrary ?org= or hostname.

CRITICAL: Add get_current_user (router-level dependencies=[Depends(get_current_user)]) to the calling, conferences, presence and reactions routers so they are scoped to the caller's org and not anonymous.

HIGH: Make the WebSocket ConnectionManager org-aware: keep connections keyed by org, broadcast/broadcast_presence/online_users only within the org, send_to_user only to users of the same org. Require a token on /api/ws. Check that chat conversation participants and task assignees are users of the current org.
HIGH: Fix login identity resolution for duplicate emails across orgs: iterate over all matches and verify the password against each; if more than one matches, require a hostname or org choice.
Proxy hardening: override or deny bulk_write, find_one_and_replace, *_raw_batches and watch; rewrite $lookup/$unionWith/$graphLookup/$facet sub-pipelines with an org $match.
Import: strip is_default from the imported org record.
Clear active_organization_id on logout (or keep it per session) so the super admin is asked to pick an org at each login, as the spec requires.
Add a SuperAdmin route guard on /organizations; add page padding to OrganizationsPage.
critical_code_review_comments: org_scoped_db.py: aggregate() prepends a $match on the base collection only. Joins into other collections ($lookup etc.) are not scoped.
org_scoped_db.py: __getattr__ passthrough exposes unscoped raw methods (bulk_write, find_one_and_replace, raw batches, watch).

Every route that does not call get_current_user is pinned to the hostname, ?org= or default org. Routers with zero auth: calling.py, conferences.py, presence.py, reactions.py, seed.py, google_auth.py (and i18n/cron, which are fine).
routers/websocket.py and presence.py hold process-global in-memory state (active_connections, user_presence, board_rooms, typing_users) that is shared across tenants.
deps.get_current_user does not reject users with status 'pending' (forged Google users are created as pending, yet their token works).
deps.py raw_db uses os.environ.get('DB_NAME', '5812global') with a default value; guidelines say no defaults.

success_rate.backend: 90% (37/41 pytest; 4 failures are real security bugs, plus manual WS/chat/calling/seed findings)
success_rate.frontend: 95% (all requested flows work; minor route-guard and design issues)

seed_data_creation: Temporary orgs test-iso-*, test-iso-*-1 and test-ui-* were created and then suspended and deleted. Temporary TEST users, members, tasks and chat conversations were deleted. A forged-Google Guest user was deleted. The owner's active_organization_id was restored to 58:12 Global. Only 5812global and lubwamas remain.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: pytest backend/tests/test_iter393_org_isolation_adversarial.py backend/tests/test_iter392_org_isolation.py. The 4 currently failing tests (calling unauth, same-email login, super_admin escalation, google forgery) should pass after the fixes. Hostname tests must hit http://localhost:8001 with a Host header because Cloudflare 403s a spoofed Host on the public URL. To re-check the WS cross-tenant leak, connect wss://.../api/ws/<58:12 admin id> and wss://.../api/ws/<lub admin id> and confirm the online_users lists are disjoint. Do not execute POST /api/seed. Clear login_attempts and set the owner's active_organization_id to None to force the picker.
rca of the issue: The proxy isolates correctly once an org is pinned from an authenticated user. The holes sit outside it: (a) role assignment never treats super_admin as a platform-level role; (b) the auth routes (google, seed) and the no-auth routers inherit the default org from the middleware fallback; (c) in-memory WebSocket and presence state never passes through the DB proxy; (d) the single pre-auth identity query uses find_one across tenants.
